review.material: The complete public chapter text and 25-page PDF were read. The rule descriptions, relative-time definitions and Fig. 9 computation were inspected.
review.limitations: The author explicitly states that the Glarner process is speculative: no recordings establish how he actually drew. No timed human experiment validates the duration model.

sections.title: What it is about
sections.text: Knight extends making grammars from describing what happens during drawing to comparing how long alternative sequences might take. A hypothetical grammar for preparatory drawings in Fritz Glarner’s Relational Painting style separates seeing/deciding from drawing/erasing.

sections.title: Central question
sections.text: Can a grammar represent duration as well as spatial change? The chapter treats creative making as a process unfolding in time, asking how different ways of reaching a similar final drawing can have different temporal structures.

sections.title: How the model works
sections.text: Five stages establish a boundary, subdivide rectangles, add oblique divisions, add wedge borders and finish. Rules alternate sensing and doing states. Gesture time is approximated by stroke length; decision time uses a provisional visual-complexity measure or assigned constants. These are relative model units, not seconds.

sections.title: The worked comparison
sections.text: Two sequences create the same orthogonal subdivision with reported relative totals of 1490 and 2082. Different intermediate area distributions change the model’s decision-time cost even when the final drawing agrees. Later examples extend the computation through oblique lines and borders.

sections.title: What is demonstrated
sections.text: The framework can make the order and duration assumptions of a drawing process explicit. Within this model, alternative sequences can differ in decision cost while keeping gesture length fixed. The result is a demonstration of representational possibilities, not a discovery of Glarner’s real working time.

sections.title: Important qualifications
sections.text: No empirical record of Glarner’s drawing process is available. The complexity measure is a placeholder; constants are chosen for comparison, and backtracking to earlier stages is excluded. The author says real drawing speed could depend on further factors and would require empirical study.

sections.title: How to experiment with it
sections.text: Describe a drawing twice: once as a finished composition, once as a sequence of looking, deciding, marking and revising. Label every timing assumption. Compare sequences under the same assumptions, and keep simulated duration separate from observed duration.
